model: Broker FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (bank-style, net debt held at zero, engine route) with deal-completes vs deal-breaks overlay

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR note 31: equity-settled share option scheme (expired 2020) with no expense recognised in FY2025; the share award scheme expense is inside staff costs and therefore inside the NI-based flow. Charged once, within earnings; sbc_pct_path held at 0.
inputs.share_count_basis: 9,529.945m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim report p.31, no treasury shares) plus 1.286m dilutive share options from the interim diluted-EPS note = 9,531.2m fully diluted. Held flat: the only equity-settled scheme is immaterial (options outstanding 4.85m, 0.05% of shares) and buybacks are negligible.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY in HKD (the flows are FCFE to ordinary shareholders): HKD 10-year government bond ~3.6% (HKD is pegged to USD so the curve tracks UST less a small spread) + 6.0% equity risk premium for a Hong Kong/China capital-markets exposure x beta 1.3 for a 12x-nominal-leverage, wholesale-funded trading broker = 11.4%, rounded to 11.5%. One point above the 10.5% used for China CITIC Bank (0998.HK) because a securities firm's earnings are mark-to-market and swung from HK$80m (FY2022) to HK$1,345m (FY2025); same rate in all three scenarios so risk is charged once, through the probabilities.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (HK$20.5m) are immaterial and inside the NI-based flow; not deducted again.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders (FY2025 HK$1,345.4m of HK$1,346.7m total profit; NCI HK$114m of HK$16,301m equity). NCI share of profit is ~0.1%, so the engine's PBT x (1 - tax) ties to attributable NI within rounding; no separate NCI deduction (charged once).
inputs.notes: MODEL: broker/securities-firm FCFE capitalised at cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF engine with a bank mapping, PLUS a deal-completes/deal-breaks overlay in `corporate_action` because the company is under a live pre-conditional privatisation scheme (HK$3.00 cash per share from parent Guotai Haitong, announced 7 Aug 2026). ROUTING: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes banks/deposit takers and brokers away from owner-FCF (OCF swung -HK$8.3bn FY2025 / -HK$23.2bn H1 FY2026 on client and trading balances and is meaningless as owner earnings) and routes a live scheme to deal-weighting; precedents GEN.NZ, LYG, WF, 0998.HK (FCFE-at-CoE, net_debt=0) and EZJ.L (standalone weighted_iv + corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenue (commission + interest + trading/investment income); `ebitda_margin_path` = PRE-TAX PROFIT margin (D&A and SBC paths are 0, so EBIT = PBT); `cash_tax_rate_path` = effective tax (HK 16.5% statutory, FY2025 effective 21.8%, H1 FY2026 15.4%); `capex_pct_path` = EARNINGS RETAINED to support balance-sheet growth and regulatory capital (the broker's 'reinvestment'), set so that terminal retention x ROE = terminal growth and so that the implied payout sits at or above the Board's >=30% dividend-policy floor (FY2025 actual 50%, FY2018-25 cumulative 65%); `wc_capture_pct` = 0. FCFE = PBT x (1 - tax) - retained earnings = dividend capacity. NET DEBT = 0 by the bank convention: the HK$36.2bn of borrowings and MTNs, HK$35bn+ of repo obligations and client payables are OPERATING funding of the trading book and client-driven financial products, not a claim to subtract from an equity flow; the HK$4.98bn cash is working liquidity. Gross figures are kept in gross_borrowings_memo / cash_memo for the reader. ROE: the model is anchored to this company's actual ROE on ORDINARY equity (NI attributable / ordinary shareholders' equity): FY2018 7.4%, FY2019 8.1%, FY2020 11.8%, FY2021 7.2%, FY2022 0.5%, FY2023 1.4%, FY2024 2.3%, FY2025 8.7%, H1 FY2026 8.4% annualised; 8-year average ~5.9%, mid-cycle ~7-8%. With ROE below the 11.5% cost of equity, fair standalone value is below book: (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) = (7.8 - 3)/(11.5 - 3) = 0.56x book in the base case, which the engine reproduces independently. LAST_FCF is FY2025 dividend capacity (NI 1,345.4 x 50% payout = 672.7), not reported FCF; the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income does not apply on this route. The 52-week high of HK$4.24 was the mid-2025 virtual-asset-licence rally; the stock was HK$2.08 on the last day before the scheme halt and HK$1.1-1.3 (0.7-0.8x book) through 2023-24.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle revenue growth. Equity 5yr CAGR (1.0%) is depressed by the FY2022-24 trough and 65% payout; revenue 5yr CAGR 5.0% and FCFE (dividend) 5yr CAGR 5.2% bracket it. 3yr figures are measured from the FY2022 trough and are not a trend.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.0-2.3%) diverges >30% from revenue (5.0% / 39.1%) and EPS (-3.4% / 160%): the business grew on leverage (equity/revenue fell from 3.6x FY2018 to 2.2x TTM; gearing 2.22x at H1 FY2026) and the base period FY2022 was a near-zero-profit trough. Mid-cycle growth selected, not either endpoint.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the FCFE proxy (dividends paid: FY2020 517, FY2022 478, FY2025 667), not reported FCF, which is dominated by client and trading balance swings (-15.1bn FY2020, +5.8bn FY2021, -8.3bn FY2025).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin. FY2026 at 21% = H1 FY2026 actual (20.7%: costs +41% on balance-sheet expansion, financing cost HK$1.66bn); normalising to 22%, the FY2018-25 average (21.1%) with FY2025's 27.7% treated as a strong year, not the run-rate.
base.capex_note: Retained earnings. FY2026 retention 8.9% of revenue = 52% of NI (FY2025 payout 50%; no interim declared because a dividend would cut the scheme cancellation price); glides to 6.8% = 38% retention = terminal g 3.0% / terminal ROE ~7.9%, i.e. payout ~62% in line with the FY2018-25 cumulative 65%.
base.growth_note: FY2026 +20%: H1 FY2026 revenue +37% YoY on an H2 that merely matches H1 (TTM already 7.28bn, +17% on FY2025). Then fades to 3% HKD nominal — HK capital-markets activity is a cycle, not a trend.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin 26% — between the FY2019 (23.7%) and FY2025 (27.7%) good years, below the FY2020-21 peaks (37%, 32%). Terminal ROE ~10.5%, still below the 11.5% CoE.
bull.capex_note: Retention 7.0% of revenue terminal = 33% of NI = g 3.5% / ROE 10.5%; payout ~67%.
bull.narrative: Standalone bull: the HK IPO/ECM revival and cross-border financial-products book (HK$89bn, +88%) compound for several years.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin collapses to 8% in FY2027 (FY2022-24 actuals were 1.2%, 5.9%, 8.3%) as trading/investment income reverses on the enlarged book, then recovers only to 16% — a structurally lower-return, higher-cost franchise.
bear.capex_note: Retention stays near the Board's 30% payout floor in the trough years (70% retained of a small NI), then 5.2% of revenue terminal = 40% retention = g 2.5% / ROE ~6.3%.
bear.narrative: Standalone bear: the FY2022-24 cycle repeats on a balance sheet now 12x levered, with margin-loan and mark-to-market losses on the HK$140bn of financial assets.

scenario_narratives.base: STANDALONE (deal-breaks world). FY2026 lands near FY2025's profit (H1 NI HK$675m, +23%) on 20% higher revenue and a compressed 21% pre-tax margin as financing costs on the 41%-larger balance sheet bite. Thereafter HK capital-markets activity normalises: revenue growth fades from 6% to 3%, pre-tax margin settles at the 22% cycle average, ROE on ordinary equity ~7.9%, payout ~62%. Because ROE stays below the 11.5% cost of equity, retained earnings earn less than they cost and fair value sits at ~0.6x book — where the stock traded (0.7-0.8x) through 2023-24 before the mid-2025 virtual-asset rally.
scenario_narratives.bull: STANDALONE bull. The HK IPO/ECM revival (record HK$286bn raised in 2025, +22% in H1 2026), Bond Connect Southbound and Wealth Management Connect expansion, and the cross-border financial-products book (HK$89bn, +88%) let revenue compound 8-10% for three years with pre-tax margin at 26% — FY2019/FY2025-type conditions sustained. ROE reaches ~10.5%, close to but still below the cost of equity, so fair value is ~0.9x book. The HK$3.00 deal price (1.8x book) is NOT reachable on fundamentals in any standalone case; it is paid for synergy and simplification by the parent.
scenario_narratives.bear: STANDALONE bear. The FY2022-24 cycle repeats — China property/credit stress, HK turnover collapse, structured-note and fixed-income marks reverse — but on a balance sheet that is now 12.4x nominally levered (8.7x a year ago) with gearing 2.22x and wholesale MTN/GSN funding. Pre-tax margin drops to 8% then recovers only to 16%; dividends are cut to the 30% policy floor. Fair value ~0.3x book; an equity injection from the parent is the realistic end-state rather than insolvency (parent ownership 65.5%, stable BBB+/Baa2).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weights describe the STANDALONE distribution, i.e. the world in which the scheme lapses. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because earnings are mark-to-market on a book that has grown 41% in six months, the FY2022-24 trough was three consecutive years of near-zero ROE, and a lapsed scheme would itself coincide with weaker markets or a regulatory refusal. Bull cut to 25% because the bull case needs the HK ECM cycle, cross-border product demand and funding costs all to cooperate for several years. The actionable number is corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv, which weights this standalone value against the HK$3.00 cash offer.

corporate_action.type: pre-conditional privatisation by scheme of arrangement (Companies Ordinance s.673), controlling shareholder as offeror
corporate_action.offeror: Guotai Haitong Financial Holdings Limited (wholly owned by Guotai Haitong Securities, 601211.SH / 2611.HK), holder of ~65.5%
corporate_action.announced: 2026-08-07 (joint announcement; request to the Board dated 2026-07-22)
corporate_action.price_basis: 44.2% premium to the HK$2.08 pre-halt close, 46.5% to the 30-day average, 37.7% to the 60-day average; ~1.8x FY2025 audited book (HK$1.66/share), 1.77x H1 FY2026 book (HK$1.70). Cancellation price is reduced by any dividend paid — hence no H1 FY2026 interim dividend.
corporate_action.scheme_shares: ~3.29bn shares (34.47% of issued capital) held by disinterested shareholders; ~HK$9.9bn consideration
corporate_action.conditions: PRE-CONDITION: PRC regulatory approvals/filings (Shanghai SASAC completed per the latest joint announcement; NDRC registration and SAFE filing outstanding). Scheme document despatch deadline extended to 2026-11-07 (or within 7 days of the pre-condition being satisfied). SCHEME CONDITIONS: approval by >=75% of votes cast by disinterested shareholders at the court meeting, votes against not exceeding 10% of all disinterested shares (Takeovers Code Rule 2.10), High Court sanction, and the offeror's own shareholder/regulatory consents.
corporate_action.status_as_of: 2026-10-17: pending; pre-condition not yet satisfied; no scheme document or court-meeting date yet.
corporate_action.expected_completion: Q1 2027 (court meeting ~Dec 2026 / Jan 2027 if the scheme document goes out by 7 Nov 2026); ~0.4 years from the valuation date
corporate_action.deal_weighted_entry_price_formula: 0.85 x 3.00 / 1.15^0.4 + 0.15 x standalone weighted_iv — the price that returns the 15% hurdle on the deal-completes leg
corporate_action.probability_rationale: 85% completion: a 65.5% SOE parent privatising its own HK subsidiary with PRC approvals that are procedural (Shanghai SASAC already done), a 44% premium, an independent financial adviser (Altus Capital) appointed, and a market spread of only ~4% — all point to completion. The 15% break risk is (a) the Rule 2.10 blocking threshold: 10% of disinterested shares (~329m shares, ~HK$1bn) voting against is a low bar for a stock that traded above HK$3.00 as recently as mid-2025 (52-week high HK$4.24), and (b) NDRC/SAFE timing slipping past the extended deadline. Set at EZJ.L's 85% rather than the market-implied ~95%+ because minority 'bump' campaigns against HK SOE-parent schemes do succeed in blocking without producing a higher price.
corporate_action.market_implied_note: At the current price (inputs.current_price) the market is pricing near-certain completion: with a HK$2.08 pre-announcement fallback the implied probability is ~100%; with the model's standalone fallback it exceeds 100%. Buying at the current price pays a ~4% spread to the offer for ~65% of downside to standalone value if the scheme lapses.
corporate_action.action: Re-run this valuation the day the scheme completes (ticker then dies — remove as EA/BEZ.L/SDR.L) or lapses (standalone weighted_iv becomes the headline). The deal_weighted_iv goes stale the moment either happens.

entry_price.method_note: Engine entry prices are STANDALONE: the price at which the FCFE path plus a terminal value rebuilt at 15% returns 15%. For the actionable deal-weighted entry price see corporate_action.deal_weighted_entry_price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A securities broker is valued on the dividends its ordinary equity can sustain, discounted at the cost of equity; reported FCF is meaningless here and borrowings are operating funding, so net debt is zero. Guotai Junan International's ROE on ordinary equity has averaged ~6% over eight years and ~8% mid-cycle against an 11.5% HKD cost of equity, so on fundamentals it is worth 0.3-0.9x book (HK$0.45-1.5/share), ~HK$1.0 weighted. The HK$3.00 parent privatisation at 1.8x book is the only reason the stock trades near the offer price. The valuation therefore has two layers: the standalone probability-weighted IV (what you own if the scheme lapses) and the deal-weighted IV (85% x PV of HK$3.00 + 15% x standalone). At the current price the market is paying for near-certain completion; the 15% hurdle is not met on either layer.
key_risks_to_valuation: Scheme lapses (NDRC/SAFE registration not obtained by the extended deadline, or >10% of disinterested shares vote against): price reverts toward standalone value, ~HK$1.0 weighted, 65% below the current price.
Scheme completes: capped at HK$3.00 (a low-single-digit spread above the current price), with the cancellation price reduced by any dividend declared in the interim.
Standalone ROE: every 1pt of sustained ROE is worth ~HK$0.2/share at an 11.5% CoE; the FY2022-24 trough shows ROE can sit near zero for three years.
Leverage: nominal leverage 12.4x and gearing 2.22x at H1 FY2026, wholesale MTN/GSN-funded; a funding or mark-to-market shock would force the bear path and possibly a parent capital injection.
Cost of equity: at 10.5% (CITIC Bank-level) the standalone base rises ~15%; at 12.5% it falls ~12% — the conclusion does not change at any rate between 9% and 14%.

data_sources.financials: 1788.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, HKD millions) from annual reports FY2018-FY2025 and interim reports H1 2024-H1 2026; balance sheet, share count and ROE anchors from the H1 FY2026 interim report (30 June 2026); dividend policy and FY2025 highlights from the FY2025 annual report.
data_sources.qualitative: 1788.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-17); interim report note 27 (events after the reporting period) and 'Dividend' section for the privatisation; joint announcement of 7 Aug 2026 and subsequent progress announcements via ACN Newswire / press coverage for the HK$3.00 cancellation price, premium statistics, Shanghai SASAC completion, NDRC pending status and the 7 Nov 2026 despatch deadline.

sanity_check_expectation: Bank/broker model: P/E and EV/EBITDA rules are not applicable (checks_replaced). Price/book on the standalone base is ~0.6x vs a 0.7-0.8x 2023-24 trading range and 1.8x at the offer; standalone base P/E on FY2025 EPS ~7x.
